findings.title: Overly restrictive type check in VisitSpeculativeAdditiveOp excludes Unsigned32 inputs
findings.message: In `VisitSpeculativeAdditiveOp`, the refactored condition `BothInputsAre(node, Type::Signed32())` is too narrow: it does not cover inputs whose type is `Unsigned32` (but not `Signed32`). The original code handled both signed and unsigned 32-bit integer inputs through the `kAdditiveSafeIntegerOrMinusZero` check (which includes the full integral32 range). With the narrowed guard, a node whose inputs are `Unsigned32` no longer enters the fast Int32Add/Sub path. Instead it falls through to a different lowering path. This produces a mismatch in `UseInfo` between the PROPAGATE and LOWER phases: the two phases assign different `UseInfo` values for the same input edge, violating the monotonicity invariant checked by `DCHECK(IsUseLessGeneral(input_use_infos_[index], use_info))` in simplified-lowering.cc, causing a crash (a DCHECK failure that in a non-debug build could silently produce incorrect code).
findings.suggestion: Replace `BothInputsAre(node, Type::Signed32())` with `BothInputsAre(node, Type::Integral32OrMinusZero())` so that both `Signed32` and `Unsigned32` inputs enter the Int32Add/Sub fast path, preserving the pre-existing monotonic UseInfo invariant across compiler phases.

ground_truth.root_cause: The restructuring in commit b663e27 narrowed the type guard from the inclusive `kAdditiveSafeIntegerOrMinusZero` (which includes Unsigned32) to the exclusive `Type::Signed32()` (which does not). This silently broke the UseInfo monotonicity contract between the compiler's PROPAGATE and LOWER phases for nodes with Unsigned32 inputs.
